title: What is daily records? A short explanation
description: What daily records means in practice, the smallest version you can try, and how your data stays stored on your device with no account needed.
answer: On Friday your daily records notes are a dozen half-finished lines with no comparable dates. GarageGo keeps daily records on-device, so it stays readable with no data plan and no account.
toc: What daily records means in practice

sections.h2: What daily records means in practice
sections.p: In practice, daily records means dated evidence you can reopen, not an intention you only remember.
Three fields only: time, status, one blocker. Everything else is optional.
GarageGo keeps daily records on-device, so it stays readable with no data plan and no account.

table.caption: A working frame for daily records

list: Pick one fixed time, not “whenever there is room”.
Open GarageGo when that time arrives, not later tonight.
Note one blocker, not a long excuse.
Back up before you switch phones.
faqs: Can I open daily records offline?
Yes. GarageGo keeps everything on-device, so no data plan is needed.
Do I need an account first?
No. Start without login; export a backup from time to time.
With the shortest piece. Add scope only after two steady weeks.
What if I miss a few days?
Do not wipe history. Resume from the last entry and note one blocker.
